comments.trustedDependencies: Bun runs no dependency lifecycle script unless the package is trusted, and declaring this field REPLACES Bun's default allow list rather than extending it -- so every package that needs its script must be named here. Only two dependencies have one: esbuild, whose `node install.js` links a standalone binary and is ABI-independent, and better-sqlite3, which is deliberately absent. better-sqlite3 is a native addon used at the BB and plain-Node compatibility boundary, and its `prebuild-install` picks a binary by the NODE_MODULE_VERSION of the runtime that executes the script. Bun reports a different Node ABI from the supported Node 22 runtime, so a Bun-run install fetches a binary that BB and plain Node cannot load. Leaving it untrusted skips that wrong-ABI download and lets the root postinstall fetch the Node binary.
comments.postinstall: better-sqlite3 is left out of trustedDependencies above, so nothing has built it by the time this runs. Invoking prebuild-install under `node` resolves the binary against the ABI used by the supported BB and plain-Node runtime. This is what `npm rebuild better-sqlite3` used to do, without needing npm on PATH. There is no node-gyp fallback here, unlike better-sqlite3's own `install` script -- a platform with no published prebuild fails loudly instead of building from source.

scripts.build: bun run build:framework && bun run --filter '@smsunarto/bb-plugin-*' --parallel build
scripts.typecheck: tsc -p tsconfig.json && bun run build:framework && bun run --filter '@bb-kit/*' --parallel typecheck && bun run --filter '@smsunarto/bb-plugin-*' --parallel typecheck
scripts.test: bun run build:framework && bun test scripts/*.test.ts && bun run --filter '@bb-kit/*' --parallel test && bun run --filter '@smsunarto/bb-plugin-*' --parallel test
scripts.clean: bun run --filter '@bb-kit/*' --parallel clean && bun run --filter '@smsunarto/bb-plugin-*' --parallel clean
